newsitem.title: USA: KDB $500 mln Yankee due, Blue Chip rolls in junk. [corrected 01:01 gmt 8/11]
newsitem.headline: KDB $500 mln Yankee due, Blue Chip rolls in junk. [corrected 01:01 gmt 8/11]

text.p: A single Yankee deal from the Korean Development Bank is expected to take center stage in the U.S. corporate bond arena as the market fades into a holiday weekend, dealers said.

The Korean concern is expected to price $500 million in A1/AA-minus 10-year debt on Thursday morning, the dealers said. The issue will be priced via lead underwriters Merrill Lynch & Co Inc and J.P. Morgan Securities Inc.
Common price talk calls for seven-year spread through 50 basis points.

Separately, YPF SA's $200 million Yankee medium-term note offering was postponed due to a recent back-up in emerging market conditions, market sources said. Merrill Lynch is lead manager on the B1/BB-minus-rated deal.
Elsewhere, El Paso Natural Gas Co is still slated to price $400 million seven- and 10-year debt this week, some said.

Dealers said issuance is otherwise thinning ahead of the Veteran's Day holiday weekend. The Public Securities Association has recommended an early close for the U.S. fixed-income markets on Friday and a full close on Monday.

High-yield issuance, while not enormous this week, is threatening to mount later this month as companies attempt to garner favorable rates and/or complete 1995 year-end finance needs, said a high-yield syndicate manager.

"What spooks people is the volume of roadshows," a manager said. "People tend not to add up the dollar volume of all the deals but they see their calendars clogged with meetings and eveybody is just tripping over one another.
Two rule 144a private placement high-yield deals priced early on Thursday.

--Blue Chip Casino Inc issued $86 million 13-3/4 percent senior secured notes due 2003 at par. The notes have a four-year equity call feature for $30 million and are rated B3 (corrects rating from Ba3) by Moody's and B-minus by S&P.
Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp is sole lead manager on the deal.

--Olympus Communications LP issued $200 million 10.625 percent 10-year senior notes at par to yield 433 basis points over the U.S. Treasury curve, a syndicate source said. The notes are rated B1 by Moody's Investors Service and single-B by Standard & Poor's.
Goldman Sachs & Co is lead manager on the deal.

In the Treasury market, prices faded ahead of the third leg of the government's quarterly refunding. The benchmark 30-year bond was quoted down 15/32 to 101-1/4 to yield 6.65 percent at 1028 EST/1528 GMT.
